run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The checkout service is down because the Deployment checkout in namespace astronomy-shop carries a pod-template nodeSelector of kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node, a hostname no node in this cluster has (nodes are sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3). Deployment checkout was (re)created/applied at 2026-11-24T10:13:44Z and updated again at 10:13:50Z, producing two new ReplicaSets (checkout-54579c864c, checkout-c69887c97) whose pods checkout-54579c864c-vdhh4 and checkout-c69887c97-bzqph are both Pending with PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable, message '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'. Deployment checkout reports replicas=2, unavailableReplicas=2, readyReplicas and availableReplicas null, and Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable); it is the only one of the 23 deployments in the namespace with Available=False. Consequently the checkout Service (ClusterIP 10.96.25.10) has an Endpoints object with zero subsets/addresses while all 22 other services have ready addresses. Traffic therefore fails: frontend spans for oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder carry rpc.grpc.status_code=14 with grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.25.10:8080 (2026-11-24T10:13:25.096Z)', frontend POST /api/checkout returns http.status_code=500, frontend-proxy POST and 'router frontend egress' spans return 500, and load-generator POST spans for user_checkout_multi/user_checkout_single return 500. Frontend container logs in the same window repeat the same ECONNREFUSED to 10.96.25.10:8080. Alternative causes were checked and not supported: no NetworkPolicies and no ResourceQuotas exist in the namespace, flagd fault flags all have defaultVariant 'off', every other deployment is available/ready, and no pod outside the two pending checkout pods is non-Running or has restarts. Startup probe/readiness noise on grafana, opensearch and the otel-collector-agent DaemonSet is early-startup transient with those pods now ready. Metric-based error rates could not be computed because the traces_* series have no samples in the sampled window.

claims.text: Deployment checkout (namespace astronomy-shop) has spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"}; it is the only deployment in the namespace with a non-null nodeSelector, and its status is Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable at lastUpdateTime 2026-11-24T10:13:50Z.

The cluster has four nodes with kubernetes.io/hostname values sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3; no node has hostname label 'extra-node', and sregym-control-plane carries the taint node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule.

Pods checkout-54579c864c-vdhh4 and checkout-c69887c97-bzqph are Pending with condition PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable, message '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/4 nodes are available: 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'; both pods themselves carry nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"} and are owned by ReplicaSets checkout-54579c864c and checkout-c69887c97, both owned by Deployment checkout.

The kubelet/scheduler recorded Warning FailedScheduling events for both checkout pods ('0/4 nodes are available: ... 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), and Deployment checkout scaled up ReplicaSet checkout-54579c864c at 2026-11-24T10:13:44Z and ReplicaSet checkout-c69887c97 at 2026-11-24T10:13:50Z; the earlier checkout pod checkout-6c769b88b5-zs64v was started at 10:13:25Z and killed at 10:13:44Z as part of that rollout.

Deployment checkout status shows replicas=2, updatedReplicas=1, unavailableReplicas=2, readyReplicas and availableReplicas null (absent), with metadata.generation 2, creationTimestamp 2026-11-24T10:13:44Z and last writers kubectl-client-side-apply (Update, 2026-11-24T10:13:44Z) and OpenAPI-Generator (Update, 2026-11-24T10:13:50Z); both current checkout ReplicaSets have the same pod-template nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node and image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-checkout.

Endpoints 'checkout' has 0 subsets and no addresses, while the other 22 services in the namespace each have at least one ready address; Service checkout is ClusterIP 10.96.25.10 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=checkout and port 8080.

Frontend spans in the window ending 2026-11-24T10:14:01Z show the checkout path failing: 5 error spans on operation oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with status rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.25.10:8080 (2026-11-24T10:13:25.096Z)', 10 error spans on POST /api/checkout with http.status_code=500, 5 error spans on 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' with http.status_code=500, 2 error tcp.connect spans with 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.25.10:8080', 5 frontend-proxy error spans on POST and 5 on 'router frontend egress' with http.status_code=500, and 5 load-generator POST error spans with http.status_code=500.

Frontend container logs for pod frontend-6859c775df-cjbdw between 10:13:07Z and 10:13:58Z repeatedly report 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.25.10:8080', with the latest occurrences at 10:13:51Z and 10:13:57Z against the checkout Service IP.

Among the 23 deployments in astronomy-shop, only checkout lacks a ready/available replica (checkout available=null, ready=null); every other deployment reports available=1 and ready=1, and every pod in the namespace other than the two Pending checkout pods is Running with restartCount 0 for all containers.
Namespace astronomy-shop contains no NetworkPolicies and no ResourceQuotas, so neither network policy nor quota exhaustion explains the checkout connection refusals or the scheduling failure.

flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) defines fault-injection flags for payment, cart, ad, product-catalog, recommendation, kafka, image load, readiness probe, LLM and email, but every flag's defaultVariant is 'off' with state ENABLED, so no flagd fault flag is switched on; paymentUnreachable/paymentFailure in particular are 'off'.

Other Warning events in the window are startup transients, not a second fault: grafana readiness-probe failures 10:13:04-10:13:06Z, opensearch startup-probe failures 10:13:09-10:13:19Z, a postgresql FailedMount for configmap postgresql-init at 10:12:59Z, and DaemonSet otel-collector-agent pod replacements (64 SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete events) around 10:13:32-10:13:38Z; those pods are currently Running and their services have ready endpoints.

Hypothesis that a dependency outage or network/quota restriction was the cause is rejected: checkout is the only deployment without available replicas, its Endpoints object has no subsets, no NetworkPolicies or ResourceQuotas exist in the namespace, and all other services have ready endpoints.

The nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node in the checkout Deployment pod template was applied by an external change tool (last writers kubectl-client-side-apply at 10:13:44Z and OpenAPI-Generator at 10:13:50Z, coinciding with the creation of two new checkout ReplicaSets); the actor and the exact command cannot be confirmed because no change-history integration is available in this Run.

Correct the checkout Deployment pod template by removing nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node (or setting it to a hostname that exists on a schedulable node, e.g. sregym-worker/sregym-worker2/sregym-worker3), then confirm that a checkout pod reaches Running/Ready, that Endpoints checkout gains an address and that frontend PlaceOrder spans stop returning gRPC 14 / HTTP 500.

gaps: No Prometheus samples for traces_span_metrics_calls_total (or any traces_*/http_server_*/rpc_*/app_* metric) exist up to 2026-11-24T10:14:01Z, so span error rates and request error ratios could not be quantified; the absence of ERROR series is unknown, not zero.

Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so what applied the nodeSelector change and when it was applied cannot be confirmed beyond the last-write managers kubectl-client-side-apply (2026-11-24T10:13:44Z) and OpenAPI-Generator (2026-11-24T10:13:50Z).
The prior checkout pod checkout-6c769b88b5-zs64v was deleted during the rollout; its container logs and its own readiness behaviour between 10:13:25Z and 10:13:44Z are unavailable.

traces_search for service checkout returned no data and 'checkout' is absent from the Jaeger service list, so checkout-side spans/errors cannot be inspected (the query returned nothing; this is not proof it made no calls).

Kubernetes events and object state only cover 2026-11-24T10:12:58Z onward for namespace astronomy-shop (the environment appears freshly started), so cluster state earlier in the 24-hour authorized window is unknown.

Whether the same nodeSelector misconfiguration exists in other namespaces/workloads outside astronomy-shop was not evaluated; only the 1 FailedScheduling event in namespace observe was seen and not investigated.
next_steps: Review who applied the checkout Deployment change (kubectl-client-side-apply / OpenAPI-Generator at 10:13:44Z and 10:13:50Z) and remove the invalid kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node nodeSelector.
After the fix, verify Deployment checkout reports availableReplicas=1, Endpoints checkout has an address, and frontend /api/checkout error spans cease.
Check whether the same fault-injection mechanism targets other Deployments in the cluster with non-existent node hostnames.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
